mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but SPX returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates easier monetary policy, boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) suggests a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth is positive but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increased industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate increased demand in the housing market, boosting related sectors and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A high CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflation, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL is high but SPX returns are positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is low but SPX returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increased retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is positive but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time.
